title: Consider a section 83(b) election after a restricted-property transfer
summary: A time-sensitive planning workflow for a US service provider who received substantially nonvested property for services from a Delaware corporation. The recipient, not the public repository, decides whether to elect and files it.
outcomes: Filed election and proof if chosen

parts.title: Identify actual transferred property, transfer evidence, consideration paid, restrictions, recipient, and dates in a private record.
parts.guidance: Use executed equity documents, payment evidence and company records to establish what property transferred, to whom, for what consideration and subject to which restrictions. Resolve conflicting dates; incorporation, signature and vesting commencement do not automatically establish the transfer date. Give the recipient and adviser a factual transfer record with any remaining uncertainty explicit, keeping sensitive evidence in the recipient’s private tax file.

execution.rationale: The authored work for “Identify actual transferred property, transfer evidence, consideration paid, restrictions, recipient, and dates in a private record.” is preparation, analysis or editing of supplied records with text, file or code tools. Any named human decisions and subsequent external actions retain their existing gates.

parts.title: Have the recipient and tax counsel assess eligibility, tax consequences, whether to elect, and the official filing deadline; flag the short window immediately.
parts.guidance: Ask the recipient’s tax adviser to assess eligibility, current tax cost, forfeiture consequences and whether an election suits the recipient’s circumstances. Use the documented transfer, restrictions, value and amount paid. Check the deadline immediately: IRS instructions specify thirty days after transfer, with the stated weekend and holiday adjustment. The recipient decides whether to elect with a clear understanding of the consequences and available filing window.

execution.rationale: The documented “Have the recipient and tax counsel assess eligibility, tax consequences, whether to elect, and the official filing deadline; flag the short window immediately.” work uses digital records, an online service or a remote communication channel and retains its named human owner. Agent assistance does not transfer the human decision, identity or signing responsibility.

parts.title: If the recipient elects, prepare current Form 15620 or a compliant statement; verify content, signature, address, and copies.
parts.guidance: If the recipient elects, complete current Form 15620 or a compliant statement using the taxpayer details, property, transfer date, taxable year, restrictions, value and consideration. Check quantities and arithmetic against the equity records. The recipient reviews and signs the election; the filing copy should be ready for the verified IRS destination, with the required recipients’ copies and the filing deadline identified.

execution.rationale: The applicable signing, filing or delivery procedure determines the medium for “If the recipient elects, prepare current Form 15620 or a compliant statement; verify content, signature, address, and copies.”. The retained evidence permits or requires resolving a jurisdiction-specific method before choosing Human Online or Human Offline. Preserve the human signatory, adviser and submission proof.

parts.title: Recipient sends the signed election using the currently confirmed IRS filing method and preserves proof of timely filing.
parts.guidance: The recipient or their specifically authorized filer submits the signed election using the current IRS instructions and verified destination. Keep the filed version with evidence of timely dispatch or other accepted filing, and follow delivery failures promptly with the tax adviser. The recipient’s file should establish what was filed, where and when; a prepared form or completed provider task alone does not establish submission.

approval.scope: specific election and filing method after tax review

execution.rationale: The applicable signing, filing or delivery procedure determines the medium for “Recipient sends the signed election using the currently confirmed IRS filing method and preserves proof of timely filing.”. The retained evidence permits or requires resolving a jurisdiction-specific method before choosing Human Online or Human Offline. Preserve the human signatory, adviser and submission proof.

parts.title: Send required copies to the service recipient and, when applicable, a different property transferee; retain private delivery proof.
parts.guidance: Send the filed election’s required copies to the person for whom the services were performed and, if different, the property transferee. The recipient or their authorized filer should use verified contacts and a secure delivery method for this tax information. Keep delivery evidence with the election and resolve failed deliveries so the required recipients receive the same filed version.

links.when: The eligible recipient affirmatively chooses the election after tax review.

metadata.reviewer: Starter editorial review; independent US tax counsel review pending

exclusions: Mere grant of an unexercised stock option

metadata.trigger: The actual date substantially nonvested property was transferred to a service provider; do not substitute vesting start, board consent, or document-signing date without review.

decisions.question: What is the legally relevant actual property transfer date and is the property substantially nonvested?
Should this specific recipient make an 83(b) election given valuation, tax cost, possible forfeiture, and other circumstances?
What is the filing deadline and correct IRS destination under current official instructions?

stop_conditions: A filing deadline may have passed
Eligibility or property status is uncertain
The recipient does not affirmatively choose the election
The form or IRS address has not been checked against current official instructions
metadata.automation_boundary: An agent may alert and draft but cannot choose, sign, mail, electronically transmit, or send copies for the individual without case-specific authorization.
